judge_assessment.explanation: I verified all twelve independently: 11+10i; i^23 = i^3 = -i; +/-7i; 3+/-4i; (1+4i)^2 - 2(1+4i) + 17 = 0; 2, -2, 2i, -2i; -2+/-3i; 0, +/-2i; (-3-4i)^2 + 6(-3-4i) + 25 = 0 (Ben's 32 is the i^2 = +1 value); (x^2+4)(x^2-1) giving +/-1 and +/-2i; (4 +/- 8i)/8 = 1/2 +/- i; and the synthesis factors as (x^2+9)(x-1)^2, so the judge's claim about the zeros +/-3i and 1 with multiplicity two is exact. Two things the judge did not check. First, problem 12 also asks "Say which solution is repeated", and the verify entry is a `zeros` check whose expected list [1, 3i, -3i] carries no multiplicity - so the delivered Quick Answers row reads "12. 1, 3i, -3i" while the key body says "x = 1 (double)"; the multiplicity claim, which is the point of the synthesis item, is unverified and invisible in the grading column. Problem 8's "State how many zeros the degree of the polynomial promises" (3) is unverified in the same way. Second, problem 9 asks the student to "state in one sentence what Ben did wrong" and this run recorded zero manual items.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 5 and 9 are a matched pair built on one misconception: both are substitution checks, and the declared trap on 9 (32, from squaring with i^2 = +1) is the same error the trap on 5 describes - so a student who passes 5 and fails 9 has a locatable slip rather than a bad day.

Problem 11 is chosen so the answer is 1/2 + i, and the key names the exact wrong answer 1/2 +/- 8i ("the 8 in the numerator was divided but the 8i was not"), which is the failure mode of dividing a complex quadratic solution by a leading coefficient.

The synthesis item earns its place: it gives one zero, forces the conjugate by the real-coefficient argument, divides out x^2+9, and lands on a repeated real zero - and the key explains WHY the conjugate is forced (x - 3i alone would leave non-real coefficients).

Every solving item is answered with a check in the key (7i and -7i substituted back, (3+4i-3)^2 + 16 = 0, the average of the roots equal to -b/2a), so the reasoning shown is verification, not just narration.

root_causes.description: The verify types available for a root question (`solve`, `zeros`) report a SET of values, so a printed question about multiplicity or about the count of roots has no representation and was left undeclared.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 12 asks for the complete solution set and "Say which solution is repeated"; verify.json id 12 is a single `zeros` entry with expected [1, "3*I", "-3*I"].
answer_key.pdf's Quick Answers row 12 prints "1, 3i, -3i" while the key body prints "x = 1 (double)" - the bank cannot show the graded part of the answer.
worksheet.tex problem 8 asks "State how many zeros the degree of the polynomial promises"; verify.json id 8 declares only the zero set [0, 2i, -2i].

root_causes.description: An error-analysis sentence was left unflagged on a run that recorded no manual items at all.
evidence: worksheet.tex problem 9 asks the student to "state in one sentence what Ben did wrong"; verify.json id 9 holds one `eval` entry.
The machine observation records gate_chain_manual_flags = false.

improvements.title: Verify (or flag manual for) every response slot the worksheet prints
improvements.proposed_change: Make the verify JSON an inventory of PRINTED RESPONSES, not of terminal answers. SKILL.md should require one verify entry per answer location a problem prints (\ansblank, \ansline, \answerline, an \underline writing rule, or a table cell the student fills), with `manual` used where the response is not a value. Enforce it with a new gate wired into scripts/build.sh that segments the worksheet .tex with tests/_tex_segments.segment_spans, counts the answer-location macros and fill-in rules per problem, and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries for the same problem id. Here problem 12 needs a declared multiplicity for the repeated root (or a second entry checking (x-1)^2 divides the polynomial), and problem 8 needs an entry for the promised root count.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet whose problem prints five \ansblank slots against a verify id carrying four entries must make the new gate exit non-zero; adding the missing entry (or a `manual` entry) must make it exit 0. Today no gate compares slot count with entry count, so the fixture passes the whole chain - the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the dominant systemic gap in this run: a sheet can no longer claim complete verification while printing blanks nothing checked, and the answer key's Quick Answers bank stops shipping short rows.
improvements.risk: Sheets that use several blanks to scaffold ONE value ("x-coordinate: __ y-coordinate: __ so P' = (__, __)") will need either a coarser blank layout or a documented per-value grouping, so the gate needs a same-value exemption to avoid false failures.

improvements.title: Record every explanation, diagnosis and named-error item as a manual entry
improvements.proposed_change: Treat an item that asks the student to explain, justify, describe, name the wrong move, or draw/mark a representation as a MANUAL response even when a numeric part of the same problem is machine-checkable. SKILL.md and references/manual-review-aid.md should state the rule, and the response-coverage gate should scan each problem segment for imperative prose asks (Explain, Describe, Say why, Which ... did, State how, Sketch, Draw and label) and fail when the problem carries no `manual` entry. Here problem 9's "state what Ben did wrong" must force a `manual` entry.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture worksheet with a problem stem containing "Explain what went wrong" and a verify id holding only `eval` entries must make the gate exit non-zero; adding a `manual` entry for that problem must make it exit 0. The fixture passes every gate today, so the test fails before the fix and passes after.
improvements.expected_impact: The manual-review list delivered in final_response.md becomes true, and graders stop treating an unreviewed explanation as machine-verified.
improvements.risk: Keyword scanning will flag scaffolding prose that is not a graded ask ("Explain to yourself why..."), so the rule needs an explicit opt-out and a short allowlist to avoid pushing authors toward manual-everything.

case_summary: Rigorous complex-number synthesis: twelve problems that vary method on purpose, all twelve results recomputed correct including the quartic substitution and the (x^2+9)(x-1)^2 factorisation, with a key that checks its own answers and names the specific wrong values. Two coverage gaps remain: the multiplicity that the synthesis item is built around is neither verified nor visible in the Quick Answers bank, and problem 9's written diagnosis is unflagged on a run with zero manual items.
